question: A 21-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit for respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. His minute ventilation is calculated to be 7.0 L/min, and his alveolar ventilation is calculated to be 5.1 L/min. Which of the following is most likely to decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation?

options.opb: Increasing the partial pressure of inhaled oxygen
options.opd: Decreasing the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Minute ventilation" -> "tidal volume x respiratory rate" -> "increasing respiratory rate increases minute ventilation" -> "increasing the respiratory rate may decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation" -> 70% CHAIN: "Alveolar ventilation" -> "minute ventilation - dead space ventilation" -> "decreasing physiologic dead space increases alveolar ventilation" -> "decreasing physiologic dead space may decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation" -> 80% CHAIN: "Respiratory depth" -> "tidal volume" -> "increasing respiratory depth increases tidal volume" -> "increasing respiratory depth may decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation" -> 70%
analysis: To decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation, the focus should be on improving the efficiency of ventilation. Physiologic dead space represents the portion of each breath that does not participate in gas exchange, so decreasing physiologic dead space would be most likely to decrease the difference between minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation.
